desc:
Gravel and dark-green weeds cover the old, decayed road. Dense bushes line it on
both sides, trying to conquer all the open space available. The trees along the
road grow like giant pillars, their gnarled trunks rising to great heights,
disappearing from sight into the darkness of the shadowy canopy. To the north,
the forest is more open, and a clearing can be seen through the trees.
name: Old Forest Road

desc:
Some old tracks are visible on the sand of the bumpy road that runs here through
a lush grove of huge beech trees. Some of the trees are really massive, so big
that the road could run directly through the trunk and still it would be just a
hole in the bark. The enormous roots are like veins on the surface of the
ground, some of them crossing the road.
name: Old Forest Road

desc:
Huge, gloomy oak trees reach over the narrow road that snakes through the
forest. Shrubs and tangled berry bushes border the road, limiting visibility to
a minimum. The surface of the road itself is dusty and sandy, and covered by dry
weeds and occasional litter that has fallen down from the engulfing forest.
name: Old Forest Road

desc:
Tall trees reach high into the sky and bend their trunks and branches towards
the centre of the road. The road appears to be very old, but, very strangely,
quite well maintained. To the east and west the road continues on through the
dark and dreary forest. Along the south edge of the road a tree wall can be
seen. Fallen trees would prevent any move to the north.
name: Dark Road through the Forest

desc:
The Old Forest Road runs through a dark grove where large, twisted trees line
the immediate border of the road. One of the gigantic oaks has fallen onto the
road and is now slowly rotting away on the path. Spider webs cover the trees,
and dead branches and other forest litter lie on the ground. To the northeast,
an opening is faintly visible in the distance.
name: Old Forest Road

desc:
To the north and southeast the forest has faded into the distance. Tufts of
green grass poke their way through the black and grey brush. Directly to the
south the forest remains dense and dreary. The flowing meadows here are much
easier to traverse, not least due to the absence of such dark thick trees.
Further east the forest seems to lighten as the meadow expands further south.
name: Old Forest Road along a Meadow

desc:
Meadows stretch along this section of the road, giving one a good view of the
surrounding terrain. The road here is composed of gravel and appears to be very
old. Although in some places large boulders rest on the road, overall it is
quite smooth and easy to travel on. It leads straight through the meadow from
east to west, where it again enters the forest, which can already be seen down
the path.
name: Road at the Edge of a Meadow

desc:
The forest road continues to the east and west. To the south, a large flowing
meadow can be seen where tall grasses sway back and forth in rhythmic motion,
giving this area a sense of calm. The otherwise lifeless meadow emits a foul
stench. To the north the mighty forest recedes.
name: Old Forest Road

desc:
The road changes a bit here. An evil power has made the trees partly destroy the
road to the east, but it seems in a better state to the west. A giant spider web
hangs on some branches, sign of the closeness of a spider lair. To the north and
east the trees look dead, but they get gradually healthier the further to the
west one looks. However, there is not enough foliage to stop the sunshine from
reaching the ground.
name: Narrow Forest Road

desc:
The grey road sometimes almost disappears admist the trees, as though the forest
wanted to absorb it. The forest is dense, here and there a trunk has fallen
across the way, but they can easily be jumped by anyone. Lots of broken branches
lie around. To the north and south stand the sinister trees of Mirkwood, the
road continues to the east and west.
name: Road through a Dead Forest

desc:
The Old Forest Road is being ruined here by the roots which are slowly working
towards taking over the land. Many cobbles are missing, and many small plants
grow between the remaining ones. To the south, the forest seems dead, the only
living plants being small ferns. The road continues both west and east, but the
trees along it to the east seem to have more leaves.
name: Old Forest Road

desc:
A clearing opens up around the road. Some missing cobbles make potholes in the
ruts that road traffic formed, but if one can judge by the plants growing
between the cobblestones, no waggon has used this road for years. The Old Forest
Road goes on to both west and east. In the west, the trees seem dead. To the
north a small hill rises above the forest.
name: Road Clearing

desc:
The road is irregular here, as some roots have grown under it, making bulges in
its surface. Some old trails lead between the trees, shortcuts across the curve
which the road makes here. The road continues to the west and to the south. To
the north, a trail snakes between tall pines. An insurmountable hedge of bushes
blocks the way to the east.
name: Irregular Forest Road

desc:
This regularly-paved road continues to the north and to the east. Two small
paths lead to the south and to the west, through Mirkwood. Trees were obviously
cut down when the road was built, hence the stumps lining the road; but the
forest came back and now trees from both sides make an arch above the road.
name: Road through Stumps

desc:
The small trail snakes through the forest between big beeches and old oaks. It
leads to the Old Forest Road to the north, deeper in the forest to the south. An
even smaller path leads to the west and disappears in the thick forest. Lots of
trunks are covered by moss, and toadstools are growing everywhere in this humid
forest.
name: Small Forested Passage

desc:
One dead tree towers up through the canopy and opens a big hole through which
light can flood down to the forest floor. The bark has at some places peeled
away from the trunk, forming handholds and allowing one to climb up the tree.
Except for this tree, all the rest here are alive and fully grown, with big lush
leaves. Lots of threads of spider-silk join some trees. The trail leads around
the dead tree to both north and west while the brambles and vines get denser in
other directions.
name: Corner of Mirkwood

desc:
The upper part of the tree is littered with the remains of an ancient spider
web. This tree-top hideout is covered with white, silky spider webs displaying
an elaborate design which is both beautiful and deadly. At this altitude the
mountains of Mirkwood can be seen to the northeast.
name: A Spider's Lair

desc:
The trees in this area have thinned out enough that sunlight is able to
penetrate to the forest floor. Due to the increase in light the ground here is
covered with a vast array of mosses and ferns. As well as a multitude of small
vegetation, a myriad of larger plant life is also present. In short, the forest
floor in this area is covered in a moist carpet of green plant life.
name: The Mirkwood Forest

desc:
The forest has now become dense with dark old larches. The ground is littered
with small dead branches and leaves which lie lifeless on the dark rich soil of
the forest floor. Brambles have overwhelmed this area, making it hard to
traverse. About twelve yards above the forest floor, leaves and branches are
intertwined into a dark, thick layer of foliage which almost completely blocks
sunlight from reaching the forest floor.
name: The Dark Forest of Mirkwood

desc:
This colossal trunk was probably uprooted by a storm, and crushed down all the
nearby trees on its way to the ground. The soil its fall threw up made a steep
ramp that rains have compacted. Further up the trunk, the sky is visible through
a gap in the foliage. To the south, the forest gets too dense to allow you to
leave in this direction. Neither to the west nor to the east is there any way to
climb off the trunk, but it might be possible to clamber over the branches to
the west, down towards the base of the tree. Between the trunk and the foliage a
large number of spider webs spread out wide. A few of them still have partly
decaying victims in them.
name: On a Giant, Fallen Trunk

desc:
The forest here is so thick and dense that all sunlight is blocked by the
towering canopy high above. The ground is full of thistles and thorns, making
movement tough and tiresome. One distinct anomaly is present: there is a massive
uprooted tree lying to the west, its bulky, cumbersome roots hanging in the air
and blocking the passage to a dark hole which opens up inside the hollow tree.
The tree and the roots are covered in spider eggs of all sizes varying in size
from a fist to a pumpkin.
name: In Front of Giant Roots

desc:
There is a small open space in the shade of a giant trunk of an ancient, fallen
oak tree. The only way out of here would be to the west, if one were to head
there, it looks very unlikely that one could come back, since the sharp branches
are angled and point west, making it far easier to go than to return. Partly
covering the ground are the skeletons of snakes in various sizes; notable are
the long, thick chain-like spines.
name: Amongst Tangled Branches

desc:
The forest has become incredibly dense. The forest floor is made of roots,
stumps and a lot of big rocks covered by moss. A natural trail weaves its way
between trees and rocks. To the south the forest is too dense to allow anyone to
pass through. To the east, jumbled heaps of branches nevertheless leave some
room to move. To the north the forest seems even darker, if that were be
possible, and definitely menacing.
name: Deep within Mirkwood

desc:
The majority of the trees in this area have one unique quality: they are
branchless. As well as lacking branches, these trees are extremely tall. Their
canopies reach so high into the sky that the tree-tops appear to spin due to the
high winds at such an altitude. To the east the forest appears to grow darker
and more dense as bushes and other forest floor vegetation reemerge. To the
north trees become less numerous but the vegetation in this area becomes vast
and dense, creating a thicket which presents a major problem to the
unexperienced traveller.
name: Branchless Forest

desc:
Beech trees abound in this corner of the forest, amidst dry ground covered with
small green bushes. A narrow largely overgrown trail leads toward the north. The
other part of the trail has been reclaimed by the forest and no hints of it can
be seen. Some trunks of the large beech trees here have a purple sheen to the
bark. To the west of the faint path, there is a large anthill and some rocks.
name: Overgrown Path through Mirkwood

desc:
This thicket is dark and dense, with masses of shrubs and bushes which reach
five feet into the air. A small part of the forest floor is visible, with small
tufts of grass hiding between the bushes and shrubs. Some beech trees fight for
ground with the thicket. The ground is soft and damp; branches from bushes reach
out and scrape the traveller. To the south, the forest changes: the trees there
lack any branches, giving an impression of openness.
name: A Dense Thicket

desc:
The ground here is wet from the moisture which lingers in the air. The soil is
black as night, a sign that this is rich healthy soil for growing things, and
indeed an array of plants thrives on the forest floor, ranging from beautiful,
colourful flowers to simple green and black molds. To the south the forest gains
strength as it becomes denser and more treacherous. Traces of what may have been
a forest trail can be seen on the ground, though it is now almost completely
overgrown by an abundance of undergrowth.
name: Between Thick Branches

desc:
There are so many fallen trees here that the ground is scarcely visible. Huge
branches, half-rotten and agglomerated with old leaves and soil, form crude
gangways over and around the fallen trunks. Young trees have sprouted under the
remains of the older ones and are already growing a new layer of foilage to
conceal this green and grey landscape. To the east, it is possible to crawl
under the dead branches and enter a weird cave. The cave has dusty old spider
webs hanging like drapery in the entrance, partly concealing it. To the south
and to the north, the forest is too dense to allow anyone through. In the west,
there are less branches and trunks, and a trail is visible under the dead
leaves.
name: The Twisted Forest Floor

desc:
There is a wide open space inside this dead, fallen tree. The interior walls
have been emptied of its pith by insects which left only the very hard bark. To
the east the trunk ends at a network of tangled roots, and there is a small
crater under the stump. Inside the crater lies a spider's victim, mummified in
webbing. To the west, just before leaving the bark, the wood seems burnt, maybe
due to a lightning strike. The border between the trunk and the branches to the
west is not easy to see.
name: Inside a Tree

desc:
The surrounding forest is composed primarily of large black firs. The trees look
strange: they have no needles, and their dark barks have been disfigured. Some
trunks have fallen down, while others have strange roots which intertwine with
each other and dig deep into the forest floor, making travelling very difficult.
Numerous spider webs litter the canopy. The forest opens slightly to the east
and south where the trees are mainly oaks and beeches.
name: A Menacing Forest

desc:
A huge, flourishing tree stands tall among dead but still menacing-looking black
trees. Its branches, decorated by the remains of spider webs, are very
impressive and seem to move slightly independently of wind's blowing. There is
some open space to the west while to the other directions the vegetation looks
too dense to allow anyone to pass easily through.
name: A Baleful Forest

desc:
The forest is very dense and the ground sometimes seems marshy. It is quite
impossible to leave the narrow trail which snakes between the trunks. To the
west, some old, dead roots are entangled with huge bushes. To the north and
east, the Old Forest Road extends its grey shape, barely visible between the
trees.
name: Beside the Old Forest Road

desc:
The open meadow provides an uninterrupted view to the sky, a rare sight in
Mirkwood. To the north the Old Forest Road can be seen winding to the east and
west. The ground slopes to the southeast here, and gets increasingly more moist
as one moves to the west. The dark forest stands at the southern edge of the
meadow, although there seems to be a narrow gap between the trees.
name: Edge of a Wild Meadow

desc:
This corner of the meadow slopes slightly downhill, leading towards the trees in
the south. The ground gets marshier on the southern side of the meadows, and
deep animal tracks can be seen in the soft black earth. Thick black tangles of
roots and vines make their way up the slope toward the southern edge of the
flowing meadow. A young sapling sprouts in the southeast edge of the meadow, an
indication of invasion by Mirkwood from the south.
name: Wild Meadows

desc:
A grove of trees is spaced out here, along the edge of a meadow which continues
to the east. Each of the five trees has a slightly different appearance: one has
a deep, thick bark with red edges; another, a thinner shinier bark with white
accents. They stand in a rough ring shape, and their creaking in the wind makes
it seem as though they are talking to one another. To the north a road can be
seen continuing to the east and west.
name: The Foreboding Trees

desc:
An odd fog engulfs the forest floor. Thick blankets of warm fog push out and
wrap around the passerby as they seem to glide over this forest floor anomaly.
To the touch, the fog is oddly warm and moist. Underneath the white covering,
the forest floor is damp and covered with molds and fungi which leach off the
moisture in the air. To the west the fog appears to rise from the forest floor
up into the forest, reaching high into the canopy. In the south the fog
dissipates and a faint opening can be seen.
name: Foggy Tree Line

desc:
The black and dark-grey boles of the ever-bending and twisting woods close in,
shadowing the shrub-covered ground and limiting visibility. A skeleton is lying
against a huge trunk, its pale bones contrasting with the deep, dark colours of
the surrounding forest. To the south the forest opens up into a glade, while to
the north one could continue travelling deeper into the forest.
name: Dark Woods

desc:
Beech trees grow in abundance in this area, their long branches reaching upwards
and blending in to the canopy. Dense undergrowth, composed of thick ivy, shrubs
and thorn bushes, covers the ground. However, to the north the dense vegetation
clears slightly, giving a view of a road that snakes through the oppressive
forest. To the east and west the forest seems as dark and dreary as ever.
name: Gloomy Forest

desc:
Huge oaks with thick overarching branches grow in this area of the forest. The
soil is dark and gnarled roots twist on the ground. The vegetation is dense,
especially to the north and west making it impossible to continue travel in
those directions. The faint rustling of leaves can be heard occasionally, like
small creatures moving amidst the dense vegetation.
name: Gloomy Forest

desc:
Tightly-growing, shadowy trees result in an intact canopy that does not expose
the ground to the sky above. Low branches and shrubs are covered in dark lichens
and bracket fungi. The trees are covered in spider webs and spider nests, their
small inhabitants patiently waiting for prey to become ensnared. There is a
faint trail running to the east and south that shows evidence of regular use.
name: Gloomy Forest

desc:
A faint smell of decomposition pervades the area. A gloomy, oppressive silence
hangs here underneath the forest canopy. Spider webs can be seen covering the
high and low branches of the trees, mingled with the dark lichens that are
abundant in this part of the forest. Trampled vegetation to the north suggests
the passing of creatures on a regular basis.
name: Gloomy Forest

desc:
Some ancient trees were cut down around the area, forming a round clearing in
the forest. A small shelter stands here, two entrances to the building being
visible. Leftovers and carcasses littering the ground attest to the lack of
cleanlinesss on part of the inhabitants. Dense vegetation prevents passage to
the south. To the west a faint trail, a result of the somewhat frequent passing
of creatures in that direction, is barely discernible.
name: Hidden Courtyard

desc:
This unclean, filthy, and stinking room serves as a place to prepare meals:
there is a blood-stained table, a blackened fire pit, and a rather large, and
very dirty, pot to cook meat in. The floor is covered with half-rotten bones and
other litter, the origin of which is not clear. The crude albeit sturdy walls
are made of logs and clay. The only properly-made thing in this pigsty is the
door: made of heavy material and equipped with an iron lock, it seems capable of
keeping unwanted visitors out.
name: Crude Kitchen

desc:
A rudimentary-looking tunnel runs under the ground. The floor is well-trampled,
its clay surface being smoothed and packed down over time so that it is now hard
as rock, and there is neither litter nor loose gravel on it. At the western end
of the tunnel steep stairs, made of logs and a few bigger rocks, lead to the
upper floor, and to the east the passageway continues deeper into the earth. The
ceiling is relatively high, and shows signs of erosion.
name: Rough Tunnel

desc:
The walls of this room are made mostly of branches, dirt and rocks. The flimsy
ceiling, providing some protection from the elements, seems to be designed
mostly with the intent of providing shade rather than keeping out any kind of
precipitation. Some blankets, filthy and covered with twigs and leaves, can be
seen scattered across the room. An acrid smell permeates the room, betraying the
lack of cleanliness of its inhabitants.
name: Barracks

desc:
Inside, the shelter is dark and crude, with little care taken to keep the place
clean. The walls, made mostly of thick trunks, branches and rocks seem to be
barely held together by an occasional application of thick, dark mud. The
remains of a small fire can be seen in the centre of the room. Scattered on the
floor are the remains of past meals, being finished off by small scavenging
insects and rodents.
name: Dirty Guardroom

desc:
The tunnel has been constructed with rough efficiency. The marks left by picks,
hammers and shovels are still visible on the clay walls, and only occasionally
have the builders had time and motivation to erect poles supporting the ceiling.
The tunnel splits up to the west, east and south.
name: Junction in a Rough Tunnel

desc:
Carelessly-assembled, crude shelves line the walls of this small, damp room.
There are some containers, lumps of meat and miscellaneous small items on
shelves. The ceiling is upheld by several rough pillars of wood, into which pegs
have been hammered so that items can be hung from them. The stench of mould and
rotten meat hangs in the air.
name: Dirty Pantry

desc:
This roughly-built passage runs in a north to south direction inside the earth.
The walls and the ceiling have been reinforced with occasional logs, otherwise
the the walls consist only of hard, dark clay. The floor is smooth, as though
there were regular travel back and forth. To the north, the tunnel leads to a
junction. There is some kind of separate room to the west. To the south, the
tunnel ends at a sturdy wooden door.
name: Rough Passage

desc:
This is a small room with arched ceiling and walls constructed of crude bricks.
It is being used as a storage room, and is filled with miscellaneous items such
as crates and barrels. Alas, the moisture and rot have taken their toll, and
old, decayed junk is mostly all that remains. A thick layer of dust covers the
floor and all other surfaces.
name: Storage Chamber

desc:
This room is a strange mixture of pompous decoration and filthiness. It seems to
be some sort of command post. In the middle of the room stands a desk, with some
maps and other small equipment on it. There is an empty space around the table,
and the other furniture - a weapon rack, bed and cabinet - stands against the
walls around the room. The walls are covered with colourful tapestries whose
colours are very different from each other, and many of them are dirty and
stained. A huge, rotten spider's head has been nailed to one wall.
name: Inner Quarters

desc:
The branches of dark and gloomy trees hang overhead under a shadowy canopy.
Gigantic, gnarled tree trunks and dense undergrowth prevent passage in any
direction save to the east. Large fungi grow here among decomposing branches and
logs, surrounded by a dense, continuous mat of black ferns.
name: Gloomy Forest

desc:
This part of the dark forest contains a large number of oaks and beeches.
Mushrooms grow in clusters between the beeches, taking full advantage of the
humid environment that hastens the decomposition of the abundant leaf litter in
the area. To the south the foreboding shadows of Mirkwood grow darker with
dense, thorn-covered underbrush making passage all but impossible.
name: Gloomy Forest

desc:
Gigantic branches, devoid of leaves, reach down from the canopy. Huge trunks,
covered in lichens and black shelf fungi, grow cluttered to the west, leaving no
space for passage. The forest floor is uneven at best with many roots having
grown through the tree litter that covers the ground. Among the decomposing
trees, button fungi of different kinds thrive.
name: Gloomy Forest

desc:
The forest here is as black as night. Trees are densely packed within this area.
The forest floor is completely void of all plant life; small animal tracks can
be seen on the soft, moist ground. The trees in this area are twisted together
in a manner that makes a disorienting view. The black trees look the same all
around, making it even more difficult to find a way through. In all directions
an entangled mass of branches and roots is visible, and seemingly prevents going
anywhere save to the east.
name: Blackened Forest

desc:
The forest remains dark, and the ground lacks any form of life outside of the
annelids and insects which swarm over most of the forest floor. The stench of
wet dirt and decaying leaves is heavily present in the air. Above the forest
floor giant trees block out the sun, while large vines and roots protrude from
it, making passage through this dark terrain very dangerous.
name: Perilous Depths

desc:
Several big, thick trees stand close to each other. Their rough, hardened grey
bark seems old and makes the trees look almost invulnerable. Leaves and twigs
lie scattered on the ground. The trees have thick branches just a few feet above
the forest floor making the travelling hard. A large nest can be seen far up in
one of the trees and the branches around it is so dense the sky cannot be seen.
name: Forest Floor

desc:
The branches overhead make this area very dark. Strands of moss hang from above,
nearly touching the ground. To the south, two especially large trees stand next
to each other, their branches crossing each other regularly and forming a
natural ladder. The ground is covered in a thick black mud, which smells of
herbs.
name: Deep in the Forest

desc:
Red-barked trees dominate the forest in all directions except west. A purple
lichen grows on the south-facing trunks. The air has a acrid, salty smell to it.
The ground is quite dry here, with dry brown underbrush and loose leaves that
stir in the wind. An occasional faint humming noise comes from the southeast
corner.
name: Corner of Mirkwood

desc:
A dark misty woodland continues uninterupted in all directions. Tall slender
trees of various kinds stand side by side, their trunks forming a continuous
wall of dark wood, their crowns creating an intact canopy above. Black oaks with
twisted, old branches seem to grasp at anything passing through here while dead,
dried-out birch trees stand still with their old branches looking like pointing
fingers. Leaves of different sizes and colours cover the ground and make a
crunching sound when walked upon.
name: Misty Woodland

desc:
Small animal trails wind their way through the forest. The trails are narrow and
light, and disappear here and there. Prints in the shape of boots are visible as
well, hinting that these trails are used by more than the occasional forest
animal. The footprints continue deeper into the forest to the north. While the
forest to the south is too dense for travel, a small hole can be seen in this
direction. It appears to be the exit from a massive fallen tree which is barely
noticeable due to the dark forest landscape. To the west the passage is wide
enough to be able to squeeze through.
name: Winding Animal Trails

desc:
The small hill is covered with grass in various colours such as green, red brown
and almost grey. Thick branches and underbrush obscure the way to the north, and
a dank smell and dampness seem to flow out of the forest from that direction. To
the east, at the very edge of the forest stands an especially large tree, rotten
pieces of bark sitting at its trunk.
name: Meadow along the Road

desc:
The feet of many small woodland animals have left their prints on this piece of
land. The trail weaves in and out of the dark trees, but appears to head north.
To the east, Mirkwood shows its true structure. Masses of thick vegetation block
any chance of travel there.
name: Wooded Game Trail

desc:
The trees in this area have thinned out dramatically. What trees there are have
a dull, grey appearance which could be due to the lack of those mosses and fungi
which cover the trees to the north-east. Many have dying branches, completely
devoid of leaves. Towards the south the same theme of decay appears to go on for
miles. The forest has become filled with other plant life, ranging from ferns
and grasses to, in some spots, swathes of flowers and patches of berry bushes.
To the north and east the forest begins to come alive again, the trees showing
leaves and having a characteristic black bark.
name: Withering Forest

desc:
The increase in elevation is rapid as the ground slopes heavily down to the
east. The forest floor is littered by roots and vines of various sizes. The
tall, ancient trees reach high into the sky and are so numerous that sunlight is
nearly completely blocked out. The almost total absence of light prevents small
vegetation from growing here. To the west, the forest appears to open up, while
to the north it becomes far more dense.
name: Deep Forest Prominence

desc:
Here the forest is composed primarily of tall ancient beech trees, though there
are also some oaks. The bark of these trees is dark as night, and some have rub
marks, betraying the presence of large animals. The trees are distorted and
twisted, their branches weaving together to form a canopy which allows barely
any sunlight through. To the east the forest appears to thin out and allow for
easier and a quicker pace.
name: Menacing Forest

desc:
The edge of this clearing is beginning to look more and more like the forested
area which surrounds it. Trees are now becoming numerous and have begun to grow
close together. While it is still easy to travel through, it has become more of
a challenge. To the west the forest turns as dark as night. To the south the
depths of Mirkwood are visible. Tall pines stand out above the tree line.
name: Edge of the Clearing

desc:
Tall straight trees form these woods, close to the border of a rocky meadow to
the south. Further into the forest, the darkness becomes deeper, and the
denseness of the old oak trees and thorny shrubs prevents going north or east.
The shadows beyond the trees are home to many strange creatures.
name: Edge of the Forest

desc:
The forest to the south is lighter and more spacious. The edge of the forest is
close, and trees give way to a small meadow surrounding the ancient Old Forest
Road. To the north the woods are getting darker and damp, with twisted trees and
dense bushes blocking any movement. East and west of here, the forest is more
friendly, and travel in those directions is easy.
name: Near a Forest Meadow

desc:
A large rock stands in the middle of this overgrown meadow. Moss-covered trees
are clearly visible to the north: their branches have grown so thickly together
that it appears travel in this direction would be hard. The ground is somewhat
marshy, and springs a bit under your foot. To the east and west, the meadow
continues a bit farther before being swallowed by the dark forest.
name: Meadow North of the Road

desc:
This place is well inside Mirkwood, lacking any landmarks or signs of
civilisation. At some places though, odd shapes printed into tree barks remind
one that the forest is inhabited by ancient and powerful creatures. The trees
grow denser to the west, making travel in that direction too difficult. To the
north, the spaces get very narrow, but possible to traverse. The trees around
seem to move and reach toward travellers, making it hard to tell which direction
leads where.
name: Inside Mirkwood

desc:
The ground is mostly sandy here. The forest is made up of dead-looking trees
with no leaves left. To the east however are some more lively-looking ones. Some
spider webs hang from the trees, like the ghostly sails of some ethereal ship. A
small, almost non-existing trail leads towards a huge boulder standing at the
foot of a dark wall of trees.
name: Dark Forest

desc:
This part of the forest looks dead. The forest floor is covered by a great
number of what look like white sticks. On a closer look, they seem to be bones.
The ground is covered with them, though sometimes they are partly concealed by
dead leaves and roots. There is at least one complete skeleton here, wrapped in
spider-silk. To the west, a mass of vines forms an insurmountable wall.
name: Dead Forest along the Road

desc:
Occasionally one notices strange white stones, lying around between the roots of
this dark, dead forest. Squares of bark are missing on many of the trees, as if
they had been assaulted by some evil creatures. Innumerable spider webs hang
down between the trees. The forest continues toward east and west, but the way
south is blocked by an impregnable forest wall.
name: Sinister Forest

desc:
This dense forest of pines is very dark. The ground is sandy and covered in pine
needles. Lots of ferns grow in the humid sandy soil. Trails lead to the west,
through Mirkwood. One of them snakes between the very thick forest to the Old
Forest Road. To the west, the trees seem curiosly lifeless.
name: The Depths of Mirkwood

desc:
The sea of grass is surrounded by the dark, twisted and inwards-reaching woods
on all sides except to the east, where the waves of grass continue in defiance
of the high and looming trees. The forest to the north is too dense and twisted
to allow any travelling. To the west stands an old moss-covered cottage. Even
when its roof and grey walls are growing bushes and mould, and vines have
entangled themselves with it, the walls made of sturdy logs look still intact.
There is a small overgrown path which leads from the cottage to the south where
something that could be a road can be seen through the trees.
name: An Old Cottage on the Forest Glade

desc:
Long grass stretches out all around this treeless opening, which is like a sea
of stillness within the twisted forest. The sky with all its wonders is visible
above, but this privilege is of no great extent, for the dark forest looms close
to the north and south, standing there as densely as anywhere with just barely
enough space between the dark boles to make room for passage.
name: Forest Glade

desc:
Narrow, winding, seldom-travelled trails lead through the dense and gloomy woods
further into the forest somewhere to the west while to the south the forest
opens up into a clearing of some sort. To the north a wall of dark oaks rises
above the other trees, blocking out whatever lies north of it.
name: Gloomy Woods

desc:
Deep within the dark woods is a dead-end formed by the entwined trees. The
forest in the only direction out from here, east, is not much different than
elsewhere, except that the trees do not grow so closely together as to prevent
passage for everything but small animals.
name: Gloomy Woods

desc:
The trees here are ancient and bent in this gloomy and humid forest. Some are
dark and rotten, and overgrown by younger bushes. Like everything in Mirkwood
that grows old and weak, they feed the newest generation. Here and there lie old
stone blocks, now covered in moss, that once perhaps formed part of an outpost.
Everywhere around, evil has seized power over this place, proud of its influence
on what happens in its lands. Fallen trees and thorny bushes seem to prevent
travel in the eastern or southern directions.
name: Old Stones in the Dark Forest

desc:
The dense and continuous canopy of the forest, the result of hanging vines,
thick branches and giant-sized black leaves, spreads in all directions engulfing
the area in darkness. The undergrowth is dense with patches of ivy and shrubs
growing all over. Some rocks and stones lie scattered on the ground, mostly
covered in dark moss and lichens. An oppressing silence pervades this place.
name: Gloomy Forest

desc:
The trees in this area are different than any other trees in the nearby
surroundings. They are a mixture of oaks and firs, reaching far into the sky.
The bark of these trees is an ashen grey, with lichens populating the outer
surface of the trunk. The trees have twisted together in a manner which has
created a massive forest wall, which is practically impenetrable. The branches
of the trees twist overhead, making impossible the climbing of this wall. The
ground here is warm and moist, as the evil forest protects its roots from the
sun. A small glimpse of light can seen penetrating the southern wall of forest.
name: A Twisted Wall

desc:
Here the dark woods have been forced to loosen their grip on the environment,
causing an almost serene glade to open in the midst of the more malevolent
forest surrounding it. The high grass and the absence of gnarled roots to trip
unwary travellers makes this area far easier to pass through than the forest
around it. The glade continues to the west while the forest takes over to the
north and south, though in the south the forest isn't quite as dense.
name: Forest Glade

desc:
Here, on the western side of a great meadow, bright green tufts of grass stand
out against the brown brush and dead undergrowth surrounding the trees to the
north and west. To the south, a road makes its way through the forest. At some
places, barely noticeable, very old trails start and end without any obvious
purpose, but they all seem to lead from the northwest to the east.
name: Forest at the Edge of a Meadow

desc:
The forest has overcome all surrounding terrain. The sun is unable to penetrate
this deep dark world. Evil lurks in these areas in many forms, and the darkness
seems to draw its strength from a foreign power. A very old path, invaded by
barely younger trees, wanders between the trunks, leading to a less dense forest
to the west, and into the deeps of Mirkwood to the east; brambles and fallen
trees prevent move to the south and north.
name: Path between the Trees

desc:
This part of the forest smells strongly of rotting vegetation. Branches have
fallen all about here, their twisted branchlets snapping underfoot as you walk.
Bones and various debris lie scattered on the forest floor. The bones have
obvious traces of charcoal, indicating that someone has tried to burn them. The
trees grow together very tightly in all directions but west.
name: Among the Rotten Branches

desc:
The forest is very dark and cold here, and the trees are like black giants that
look as if they extend infinitely toward the sky. The trees seem to whisper to
each other through their slow, rhythmic creaking. High up in the branches,
small, silk-wrapped cocoons can be seen hanging.
name: Whispering Mirkwood

desc:
The forest here is pretty thick and dense, and the sheer quantity of vines
hanging down from the huge oaks makes it even darker. The vines seem to protect
the old trees from danger and almost appear to react to movement within the
forest. Between two giant oaks to the north, the carcass of some long-dead
creature is suspended from snaking vines several feet above ground. In a line
running from north to south, the forest floor appears to have been disturbed.
The disturbance disappears to the south through a large cobweb that is strung
between trees.
name: Brushy Forest

desc:
The Old Forest Road has not been used for a very long time, but it is still in
very good shape here. Small breaks, which allow limited travel off the road, can
be seen to the north and south. A faint reddish trail runs between the breaks
across the road. Ancient trees tower over the road stopping any hope of direct
sunlight breaking through. The road continues to the east and west.
name: Old Forest Road

desc:
Most of the Old Forest Road is intact here. However, some of the stones have
come loose from the surface of the road and now lie scattered along the
roadside. Otherwise the road is in very good condition for travelling on foot or
on horseback. The crowns of the trees to the north reach out over the road
casting it in deep shadow. The forest blocks the way to the south.
name: Old Forest Road

desc:
Over the years wind and rain has washed away small parts of the road. Fallen
branches and leaves lie undisturbed on the road. Despite the flaws in the road's
surface, travel along the route remains quick and easy. The branches and crowns
of the trees lining the road are blocking out most of the sky.
name: Old Forest Road

desc:
The road makes a sharp turn to the north and west here. Some fallen trees can be
seen and need to be avoided. Here and there on the road, roots of the massive
trees lining it breaks the paved surface. The place has been cast into deep
shade by the thick canopy overhead and little can be heard save for the forest
creaking.
name: Bend in the Old Forest Road

desc:
The road stretches from this bend to the east and south. The road surface has
deteriorated leaving a thin layer of gravel over the remains of the paved road.
To the north, it is impossible to force a path into the forest because the trees
stand too close to each other. To the west, a dense thicket seems to have fallen
under heavy darkness, and the shifting branches seem to form grotesque shapes
that defy closer examination.
name: Bend in the Old Forest Road

desc:
The road through Mirkwood runs straight to the east and west. On the ground,
fallen branches and wilted leaves lie scattered, covering roots that encroach
onto the road from the surrounding forest. Several small ravines in the road's
surface seem to have been made by erosion. Flanking the road, black yews and
beeches rise tall, their branches reaching out above the road to cover the sky.
The road is kept in deep shadow and the only sound around here is the distant
chattering of small animals.
name: Old Forest Road

desc:
This section of the Old Forest Road runs in a straight line from east to west.
Although it was built with great skill, centuries of use have not been kind, and
the road has become rough and unkempt. The woods on either side encroach upon
the road, with dark trunks rising just feet from the road itself, looming
inwards and all but meeting above almost as if Mirkwood is poised to strike and
swallow the road in one rustling gulp.
name: Old Forest Road

desc:
The road continues east and west, lying upon a bed of solid rock apparently
carved out of the short bluff to the north. The trees and branches to the south
lean out above the road, which meet with the branches of the trees towards the
north. The dense canopy makes it very difficult to see the sky at all. To the
south of the road, the ground slopes downwards and is quickly obscured behind
large bushes covered in thick, sharp and black thorns.
name: Old Forest Road

desc:
The forest floor rises upwards slowly towards the east where a mighty tree is
visible. The trees grow thick and tall on the slope to the south; ash and oak
stand among dense groves of oddly twisted pines. The forest floor is moist and
the air clear despite hanging vines dangling like delicate webs from overhead
branches. The only evidence of activity here are small animal tracks in the
undergrowth.
name: Forested Incline

desc:
While the dense foliage makes it difficult to see, something seems to hang up
there, suspended high in the trees. There are no easy places to climb up the
looming trees though. The undergrowth shows signs of being trampled, as if this
area sees traffic from large creatures with some regularity. Thick, thorny
bushes growing between the trees prevent passage to the north and south.
name: Shadowy Forest

desc:
Two exceptionally large pine trees grow here amidst a dark forest of oak and
beech. A faint smell of decay comes from the ground where the lower layers of
needles and leaves rot beneath more recent fallen foliage. A gate of wood,
reinforced with bands of metal, is standing to the west. A high stockade
encloses the parts of the area, making it impossible to see what is inside.
Above the gate, the huge, fanged head of a spider is nailed onto a beam.
name: At a Wooden Gate

desc:
On the ground there are obvious tracks of life. There are some blood stains
leading south beneath a half-built guard house that has been erected between
three massive black oak trees. All directions, except south which leads toward a
road, seem to have been cleared at some point but are now choked off due to the
forest undergrowth having vigorously grown in.
name: Under a Half-built Guardhouse

desc:
Large beech trees stand here draped in a curtain of vines. Creepers and vines
hang from every branch with their long tendrils brushing the ground as they sway
in the breeze. For a change, the trees seem to be losing their battle with the
forest as vines twist and bend around the trunks as if trying to strangle them.
There is a palisade and beyond it wooden structures visible to the south.
name: Vine-covered Forest

desc:
This side of the outpost has a crude gate blocking the passage to the north,
keeping the animals of the forest and other creatures and potential enemies out
of the outpost. In addition, the orcs have a good control of the passage of this
part of forest with the strategic placement of the gate, and the other
structures of the outpost, such as a high stockade and crude huts.
name: North Gate of an Outpost

desc:
An area next to the main outpost has been fenced in by a solid-looking fence of
thick, crooked branches and smaller trunks. The enclosed area is located between
three big pine trees and the outer palisade encircling the whole outpost. Inside
the area, there are many gnawed bones and one bloody, half-eaten carcass of an
ox-like animal lying on the ground.
name: By a Kennel

desc:
A huge fire pit has been dug in the centre of this area. Around the pit, there
are several logs serving as primitive benches. Sticks, bones, and pots lie
scattered on the ground. A big cauldron is hanging above the fire pit, with some
foul-smelling concoction inside. Several severed appendages, looking
suspiciously like those of the great spiders of Mirkwood, stick up from the
cauldron and hang over its edge.
name: Fire Pit

desc:
At the centre of the outpost, there is an open area with no huts or other
buildings. Several wide trees have been left standing here providing some shade
while their lower branches and surrounding undergrowth has been cleared away. A
variety of objects, such as broken shields of wood, rotting carcasses of
spiders, and other junk have been nailed to the trunks. Most objects have been
thoroughly demolished by arrows and slingstones, and it is obvious that this
area is used for practicing ranged weaponry.
name: Untidy Target Range

desc:
In the midst of the trees, this miserable orkish outpost offers protection from
malicious creatures of the forest outside thanks to the high wooden palisade.
Some of the trees behind the palisade have been hacked down, but not so much as
to let the sun shine through. A rope ladder is hanging from a wooden platform
visible up in a pine tree, which is overgrown by black vines.
name: Below a Watchtower

desc:
Several shoddy huts have been constructed here, with roofs of branches and
vines, and walls made of mud and wood. A small pit for a camp fire is located
between the huts, with a few roughly-made chairs standing around the fire pit.
To the west, there is a strong wooden palisade protecting the outpost. The
apparently indifferent inhabitants of the huts have discarded trash and food
leftovers on the ground.
name: At the Outpost's Barracks

desc:
Several filthy mats and blankets lie scattered on the floor of this miserable
hut. There are no windows in the walls and only one door leading out. The roof
is made of branches and vines, held up by a few rough but sturdy beams. It is
sealed with mud in an attempt to make it weatherproof. The walls are built in a
similar manner.
name: Inside a Barrack

desc:
The crude worksmanship of this hut leaves little doubt that it is a work of
orcs. Even so, more effort has gone into it than would be typical; it is likely
the quarters of an important orc. The hut stands on a foundation of stone slabs
that, even though they are uneven, is further evidence of the effort gone into
its construction. Several furs, skulls, and other trophies hang on the walls,
and a thick mat of pelts in the centre of the room might serve as a bed, if
somewhat oddly placed.
name: A Captain's Corner

desc:
This end of the outpost has an opening in the palisade, but it is blocked by a
huge pile of garbage. The pile is obviously working as the final location for
trash, filth, bones, and food leftovers of the inhabitants of the outpost. Very
strong, foul odours waft from the huge garbage pile. A palisade is blocking the
way to the west and east.
name: Garbage Pile

desc:
Around the outpost, there is a wooden palisade built from pikes and sharpened
stakes. On a few locations along the palisade there are small platforms made of
wood and stone, providing ideal positions for archers. The palisade is
uninterrupted to the south, but to the east there is a huge wooden gate
reinforced with bands of metal.
name: Orkish Outpost

desc:
A well-hidden wooden platform has been built amidst the forest canopy; it
probably serves as a lookout for watching the road that runs through the forest
to the south. There is a rack for arrows and other weapons on the centre of the
platform, and judging from the crude craftsmanship, it is of orkish origin.
Rough as the whole place may seem, it fills its purpose perfectly. A rope ladder
hangs from the hatch in the floor.
name: Lookout in the Trees
